Background from the published record 1. Timeline of the Phase II Project (Prior Events & Commitments) Prior Events and the Visioning Foundation Cycle 86 (August 2041) — Initial Authorization: The Oakland City Council authorized Phase II of the Fruitvale Transit Hub —a $230 million investment in one of the city's most transit-dependent neighborhoods [1] . Passed with strong support from the Oakland Progressive Party (OPP) caucus and Council President Ramon Vega, the measure moved the project from completed community visioning into active design and build planning, anchored by a negotiated BART memorandum of understanding (MOU) [1, 2] . The Six Non-Negotiable Commitments: The original Cycle 86 visioning framework locked in six mandatory covenants to protect the neighborhood's existing fabric: 20% of commercial space reserved for existing local businesses at pre-development rates for 25 years [3] . A minimum 35% affordable residential floor , with full project scope targeting 67% affordability across 420 units [3] . A minimum $15 million business stabilization fund [3] (later negotiated and executed at $18 million in partnership with the Unity Council [4] ). 30% of construction jobs reserved for Fruitvale residents between the ages of 18 and 30 [3] . A 15,000-square-foot community plaza managed by the city or a local nonprofit [3] . A binding community benefits agreement (CBA) required as a legal precondition before any construction permit could be issued [3] .

The Path to the Floor and Legislative Milestones Cycle 93 — The Routing Glitch: The scheduled City Council vote on the Fruitvale Transit Hub stalled when the council’s electronic agenda-routing mechanism failed to fire across all nine offices, leaving the $230 million project momentarily frozen in administrative limbo [5, 6] . Cycle 94 — The Multilingual Breakthrough & 8-0 Vote: The project finally cleared the council floor, passing with an 8-0 unanimous vote (with one member absent) [7] . The breakthrough occurred after planning leads incorporated a 12-page scope addition detailing Mam-language wayfinding and translation services (budgeted between $85,000 and $120,000) directly into the base document to secure the swing vote of District 2 Independent Leonard Tran [8-10] . Cycle 97 — Groundbreaking: Shovels officially went into the ground on a Tuesday morning in Fruitvale, initiating the underground utility work [11, 12] . Cycle 99 — CBA Execution: The tripartite Community Benefits Agreement governing the project was officially signed and executed, guaranteeing 34 prevailing-wage apprenticeship slots , anti-displacement protections as contract conditions, and a $180,000 workforce set-aside [13] . Cycle 102 — Technical MTC Review: The project successfully cleared its scheduled technical review with the Metropolitan Transportation Commission (MTC), keeping it on track for a critical regional funding vote projected in Cycle 104 [14] .
